content: Pharmacologic therapy for adults with type 1 diabetes includes the option of beta-cell replacement therapy for individuals experiencing severe complications associated with the disease. This approach involves either pancreas transplantation or islet cell transplantation. However, these procedures necessitate lifelong immunosuppressive therapy to prevent immune-mediated rejection of the transplanted tissue. The 2021 joint report by the American Diabetes Association (ADA) and the European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) provides detailed guidance on the management of type 1 diabetes and outlines specific criteria for the consideration of beta-cell replacement therapy.
